- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to align with mean reversion.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >75), model often overshoots in the next 5–10 days; apply a downward correction of 1–3% to avoid overreaction.
- If sentiment is consistently negative (≤ -0.33) over 3–5 days, model underestimates; adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.5% to reflect potential rebound.
- Model frequently overpredicts early in the 30-day horizon when sentiment is neutral or mildly positive; cap forecast at 1–2% above recent 7-day average to avoid lagged bias.
- When sentiment shifts from negative to positive (e.g., from -0.33 to 0.67), model lags in adjusting; apply a 1–3 day lead-in correction to anticipate sentiment-driven reversal.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome is consistently below 70, model often overestimates; apply a downward bias of 1–2% to reflect lower volatility or policy tightening.
